I'm not sure if this is a legitimate question or an attempt to bash Trump in an ever-so-trendy manner, usually with an "obviously Trump supporters are idiots or senile" pretext. Could you please clarify?

I don't think it's that Trump supporters are idiots, but they are, by and large, incompetent to make governmental decisions. The guilty secret of democracy is this: most voters aren't competent to decide matters of state. Think of the average man on the street, and then remember that he's "average", which means that half the population are stupider than he is. The goal of a good democracy is to prevent the wishes of the majority of the population from coming to pass, because most of the time the majority will be in favour of the easy but incorrect solution to any particular governmental question. For example, most people (even some quite bright ones) think that economic protectionism is a good thing - protectionism looks like a good thing to most people, because it "protects" the economy and makes sure people still have jobs. However, both from a theoretical and empirical point of view the evidence is that free trade is far better than protectionism. The problem is that this can't be explained to most people, because the case is just too difficult for most people to debate. Most people don't have the necessary mathematical and other reasoning skills to more than scratch the surface of the debate. In the same way, the man on the street doesn't have the skills to decide which treaties to negotiate or sign, which health policies will save the most lives, which agricultural policy will best feed the country, and so on. The aim of most honest politicians, though they must never even hint this, is to persuade the masses that they will deliver what the masses think they want, whilst actually delivering what would be good for the masses, even if they think they don't want it. A good politician (by which I mean a reasonably intelligent person capable of subordinating their ambition to their desire to govern in the best interests of their voters) working in the economic area of government pretty much certainly has to deliver free trade, even while they may be claiming to work for protectionism. The same is true for every other area of government: politicians have to consult academics and other experts, if they don't have the necessary expertise themselves, then sell this expert guidance to the voters.

The problem with Trump is that he does not have the humility to defer to the experts. Instead, he is stirring up the incoherent masses and promising to deliver what they think they want, even though this is likely to damage the country hugely.
